newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Northwest spot power soars on weather, natgas.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Northwest spot power soars on weather, natgas.

text.p: Spot power prices in the U.S. Northwest jumped sharply amid freezing temperatures, stronger natural gas prices and unplanned power plant outages, market sources said Tuesday.
"The power is flowing from California to the Northwest," said one Oregon trader. He noted that bids at the California-Oregon border (COB) were seen at more than $50.00 per megawatt hour (MWh).
But other traders reported few actual deals at those levels, noting a few utilities looking to cover nearby needs, but not at such high prices.
Unit 4 at the Colstrip coal-fired power plant in Montana was ramping down for tube repairs, while the restart of unit 1 at the Navajo plant in Arizona was delayed until Monday.
Sources also cited vague rumors of other unplanned outages.
In addition, Bonneville Power Administration's withdrawal of surplus power offers during on-peak hours on Wednesday was said to boost the physical market.
Firm, peak electricity at COB on Wednesday was quoted $30.00-33.00 per MWh, compared with $26.00-28.00 for Tuesday.
Firm, off-peak COB power for Wednesday was quoted near $20.00, compared with around $16.00 on Monday.
Wednesday firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was pegged at $32.00-$36.00, much higher than $27.00-29.00 Monday.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity for Wednesday was quoted $29.50-$30.50, up from $27.00-29.00.
Off-peak PV for firm delivery Wednesday was quoted near $15.00-$16.00, little changed from Monday.
Wednesday firm, peak prices at Four Corners were higher in line PV at $30.00-$31.00.
Firm, off-peak Four Corners power was assessed at $15.50-$16.50, little changed from Monday.
